text:
Minnesota arrives with points in five straight (4-0-1) after a 5-1 win at Washington on Sunday, a game in which Kirill Kaprizov reached 500 career points. The Wild are without Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno. Philadelphia snapped a three-game winless run with a 6-3 win over Utah, and is without Rasmus Ristolainen. The extra story is Bobby Brink, back in Philadelphia for the first time since leaving the Flyers after 201 games.

Our numbers favor the Wild. At five on five, Minnesota has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, Philadelphia 40%, and the Flyers' 4.3 penalties a game keep handing out power plays. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt is at +10.9 goals saved above expected this season, while Philadelphia's projected Dan Vladar sits at +0.1 but has a +12.74 mark from last season, and his recent starts have been better than his .885 suggests. Our model projects 3.49 goals for the Wild and 2.55 for the Flyers.

Kaprizov is our top scoring pick at 52%, on a five-game point streak, and The New York Times ran a piece on his scoring tear. For Philadelphia, Matvei Michkov has 10 points in his last 10 games and a 27% chance to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Brink: he plays about 14 minutes on the third line, but his shots have been dangerous, and we have him at 17% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
